question: is a gen1 flight-line vertical tie a property of the LINE, or of the place it was fitted?

inputs.role: gen1 tile over the Elba study area, for the window ladder and the within-tile repeat
gen1 tile over the Elba study area, for the window ladder and the within-tile repeat

params.name: res_m
params.why: coreg.coregister_swaths / align_swaths default grid resolution (2.0 m)

params.name: exclude
params.why: coreg.coregister_swaths terrain proxy ~isin(classification,(5,6,9)) -- the VENDOR classes, so no CSF run is needed

params.name: tie_modes
params.why: the two estimators coreg.coregister_swaths supports; corrections_geoid.json records swath_tie='intercept' as the pipeline's

params.name: half_width_m
params.why: window half-width for the along-track sweep and the chains. There is NO library default and none is invented here; 400 m is one rung of the ladder in section 2, chosen so the window fits inside a single 2.5 km tile at every along-track sample. Section 2 measures what the choice costs; section 3 is re-runnable at any other rung with --half-width-m

params.name: ladder_half_widths_m
params.why: the window sizes reported in section 2. Chosen to span a factor of 12, from below one flight-line sidelap width to a whole tile; nothing is excluded on their basis, the whole ladder is printed

params.name: shape
params.why: square window. A disk would give a ragged grid edge and fewer cells for the same half-width; localtie supports both and --shape switches it

params.name: mark_radius_m
params.why: radius within which a mark's flight line is identified by return count (groundtruth.chain.covering_lines). It selects WHICH LINE the mark is on, not which marks are used; every mark is reported

params.name: repeat_step_m
params.why: along-track spacing of the within-tile repeat windows in section 3c. 300 m so that neighbouring 400 m-half-width windows overlap and neighbouring 800 m ones overlap heavily; it sets the SAMPLING of the short-range scatter, and excludes nothing

params.name: repeat_half_widths_m
params.why: the two window sizes section 3c repeats at, so that scatter which is estimator noise (shrinks with window) can be told from scatter which is local structure (does not)

params.name: centre
params.why: where each along-track window sits across the overlap strip. 'strip' is the strip's own median easting -- the sidelap middle, where the intercept tie is an interpolation; 'tile' is the overlap cell nearest the tile centre, which on a N-S strip is its western EDGE. Both are run and both are reported; neither is used to exclude anything

params.name: target_line
params.why: the frame the marks are carried into. 137 is the middle Elba line and the one the brief names; --target-line changes it

columns.half_width_m: window half-width about each sample location, m
columns.tie_mode: which coreg tie estimator produced the number, overlap_median or intercept
columns.n_windows: windows tied along the 136-137 overlap inside 4342-29-64.laz
columns.mean_mm: mean of the tie over those windows, mm
columns.sd_mm: standard deviation of the tie between those windows, mm
columns.min_mm: smallest tie among those windows, mm
columns.max_mm: largest tie among those windows, mm
columns.span_km: along-track distance from the first window centre to the last, km
